title: Four property businesses, four ways to make money
scope: A bounded public comparison of four anchor cases. It is a chapter, not an exhaustive company count or a forecast for Bangladesh.
archive_boundary: This chapter is current reviewed work for the 9 September 2026 presentation edition. The wider evidence route includes a dated archive with different review depth.

cases.name: Rightmove
cases.status: Active listed company in the reviewed period
cases.payer: Estate-agency branches and new-homes developers pay recurring packages, upgrades, data and lead products. Consumers search without being the primary payer.
cases.problem: Property professionals need repeatable demand and visibility across a fragmented supply base.
cases.workflow: Agents and developers submit structured listings. Rightmove distributes and ranks supply, sells visibility and lead products, and supports data quality and account operations.
cases.distribution: A national portal with a professional supply network. The recurring payer relationship is more important to the economics than consumer registration alone.

journey.event: Rightmove launched as a property portal.
New Homes became a separate product line.
Mobile use became larger than desktop in the company timeline.
The listed business reported recurring professional revenue, retention and profit.

cases.funding: Listed-company capital structure. A venture funding round is not the relevant comparison.
cases.undisclosed: Current churn by payer cohort, lead-to-close conversion, and the portion of revenue attributable to each product are not established by the selected source.
cases.transfer_note: The transferable mechanism is a repeatable professional payer relationship. UK density, regulation, listing quality and mature demand cannot be assumed in Bangladesh.

cases.name: 99acres
cases.model: South Asian advertising and lead portal
cases.status: Operating segment of listed Info Edge in the reviewed period
cases.payer: Brokers, builders and owners pay for listings, visibility, leads and related products. FY2025 billing mix was 63.4% broker, 28.5% builder and 8.1% owner in the annual report.
cases.problem: Searchers need broad, current inventory while professionals need qualified demand and differentiated visibility.
cases.workflow: The portal aggregates primary, secondary, rental and commercial supply, improves listing content, sells premium products, and uses on-ground sales teams across key cities.
cases.distribution: Online discovery is reinforced by mobile, content, sales coverage and city expansion. The product still bridges users to developers and agents for offline completion.

journey.event: The annual report describes a shift toward richer listing content, video, virtual tours, decision tools and lead-conversion work.
The report records 956k+ listings, 88.2k+ customers and a ground sales presence in 60 cities.
Billings grew while operating PBT remained negative, with cash from operations turning positive in the reported period.

cases.funding: Part of listed Info Edge. The selected source does not present 99acres as a separately venture-funded company.
cases.undisclosed: Customer-level renewal, lead conversion, acquisition cost by city and unit margin are not disclosed in the selected segment pages.
cases.transfer_note: India is the closer regional comparator for distribution and professional payers, but the reported loss warns that audience scale and billing growth do not settle profitability.

cases.name: Pinhome
cases.model: Integrated property, finance and home-services platform
cases.status: Operating company with a company-reported multi-product sequence
cases.payer: The public record suggests multiple payer and partner paths across property search, agents, developers, financing and home services. It does not disclose a clean group payer or margin split.
cases.problem: Property decisions create adjacent needs: agent coordination, financing, rental protection, maintenance and service fulfilment.
cases.workflow: The company timeline shows a sequence from agent tools and property discovery to home services, financing and additional transaction or service layers. Each adjacency has a different partner and fulfilment burden.
cases.distribution: A single app, agent network, bank partnerships and provider network are used as distribution claims. The scale figures are company-reported and not independent market share.

journey.event: Pinhome officially launched and introduced its property and agent product foundation.
Pinhome Service was added for household needs.
The company timeline adds iVestment and KPR Take Over.
The timeline adds further resale, rental and agent-related product work.
The market report says KPR Take Over transactions rose 5% and Sharia KPR transactions rose 4% versus H2 2024, based on Pinhome internal data.

cases.funding: Funding history and capital providers are not used as a success proxy in this chapter because the selected public sources do not provide a clean, comparable audited financing and unit-economics record.
cases.undisclosed: Audited revenue, gross margin, completed transaction count, product-level payback, provider retention and the cost of guarantees are not disclosed in the selected sources.
cases.transfer_note: The transferable lesson is sequencing and separation of operating burdens. Indonesia's bank, notary, service-provider and geography conditions are not Bangladesh defaults.

cases.name: Propzy
cases.payer: The model depended on transaction and service economics around an O2O brokerage workflow. The closure reporting does not isolate the payer or collection step as the single failure point.
cases.problem: A brokerage can promise a more trusted transaction by combining digital discovery with field sales centres, screening and human execution.
cases.workflow: Reporting described a broad field footprint, prescreened listings and human sales operations. The closure account describes staff departures, wind-down and financial hardship.
cases.distribution: Offline centres and a digital platform were combined. That reach also created a meaningful staffing and cash burden.

journey.event: Propzy was founded as an O2O residential brokerage in Ho Chi Minh City, according to later reporting.
Series A reporting described 30 sales centres, about 400 staff and a reported US$25m round.
Operations ceased after reported financial hardship and a difficult funding environment.
Additional press analysis reported workforce cuts and a heavy operating burden, but did not provide audited causal decomposition.

cases.funding: TechCrunch reported a US$25m Series A and later coverage cited total funding around US$33m. Those figures are reported funding, not proof of unit economics.
cases.undisclosed: The public closure account does not provide audited runway, contribution margin, collection rate, customer concentration or a causal ranking of failure factors.
cases.transfer_note: Use this as a cost and concentration warning. It does not prove that a narrower, better-governed Bangladeshi workflow would fail.

claims.statement: Rightmove reported £389.9m group revenue and £256.3m statutory operating profit in FY2024.
claims.note: Company results for a listed UK portal.

claims.statement: Average revenue per advertiser was £1,524 per month overall, with agency ARPA of £1,440 and new-homes ARPA of £1,987.
claims.note: The payer denominator is professional advertisers, not consumers or completed sales.

claims.statement: Existing-partner retention was reported at 90%, and membership ended at 19,047.
claims.note: Retention is a company metric and membership is not a consumer user count.

claims.statement: The durable mechanism visible here is recurring professional spend around a trusted supply and lead channel, not a transaction commission take rate.
claims.note: Interpretation, not a causal claim about every portal.

claims.statement: 99acres billings were INR 4,507.44m and operating PBT was negative at INR 475.25m.
The reported billing mix was 63.4% broker, 28.5% builder and 8.1% owner.
claims.note: A customer or billing mix is not a margin mix.

claims.statement: The annual report showed 956k+ listings, 88.2k+ customers and a ground sales presence in 60 cities.
claims.note: These are reported business indicators, not completed transaction counts.

claims.statement: The case supports a professional-payer portal model, but it contradicts any simple assumption that audience and billing scale guarantee portal profit.
claims.note: Interpretation from the reported billing and operating result.

claims.statement: Pinhome says it had more than 4.1m downloads, more than 40,000 property agents and more than 1.8m quality property listings.
claims.note: Downloads, agent collaboration and listings are company-reported. They are not active users, completed transactions or audited market share.

claims.statement: Pinhome reports a 5% increase in KPR Take Over transactions and a 4% increase in Sharia KPR transactions based on its internal data.
claims.note: Absolute transaction counts, revenue and margin are not disclosed.

claims.statement: The official product timeline shows a sequence from agent tools and property discovery to home services, financing and additional transaction or agent features.
claims.note: Sequence is visible. Product-level economics are not.

claims.statement: The useful lesson is not that a single property app becomes a super-app. It is that each adjacency adds a separate operator, partner, liability and metric.
claims.locator: Synthesis of history and H1 report
claims.note: Interpretation; it does not rank Pinhome's internal products.

claims.statement: VnExpress reported that Propzy operations in Vietnam had ceased on 12 September 2022, with the CEO confirming the shutdown.
claims.note: Closure date is reported and preserved as a dated event.

claims.statement: The closure account cites financial hardship, global instability, pandemic lockdown losses, staff departures and an inability to recover after the funding environment changed.
claims.note: These are reported contextual factors, not a measured causal ranking.

claims.statement: TechCrunch described Propzy as an offline-to-online townhouse brokerage with 30 sales centres, about 400 staff and a reported US$25m Series A; the figures were company and investor reporting at the time.
claims.note: Footprint and cumulative transaction statements are not audited outcomes.

claims.statement: The counterexample makes staffing, cash runway and concentration risk part of the venture model. It does not prove that every managed brokerage will fail.
claims.locator: Synthesis of funding, footprint and closure reporting
claims.note: Bounded interpretation; no single cause is asserted.

transfer_conditions.anchor_observation: Rightmove and 99acres monetise a professional supply base. Pinhome reports a large agent and listing network, but as company claims.
transfer_conditions.bangladesh_question: Can a defined Dhaka lane obtain fresh, permissioned units with an owner, status and next action, rather than copied listings?
transfer_conditions.what_evidence_is_missing: A dated sample of active units, duplicate rate, freshness, response ownership and paid renewal by payer.

transfer_conditions.anchor_observation: Professional payers and human field teams remain visible across the cases. Propzy shows that a broad field footprint can also be expensive.
transfer_conditions.bangladesh_question: Will agents share a mandate, document trail and fee rule when a parent-backed venture could compete with them?
transfer_conditions.what_evidence_is_missing: Signed mandate terms, agent fee split, bypass rate, complaint rate and collected commission by deal.

transfer_conditions.anchor_observation: The selected cases depend on structured supply and transaction or service handoffs. Bangladesh has a public e-mutation service, while the IMF describes experimental RPPI work.
transfer_conditions.bangladesh_question: Which document and inspection checks can be completed, rights-aware and owned by a named professional before a booking or fee claim?
transfer_conditions.what_evidence_is_missing: A legal workflow map, sample documents, verification authority, exception log and turnaround baseline.

transfer_conditions.anchor_observation: Pinhome's financing figures are internal-data claims, while Rightmove's recurring payer model avoids carrying property inventory. Propzy's closure warns against hiding funding needs inside operations.
transfer_conditions.bangladesh_question: Who pays, at what event, under what written mandate, and who owns non-collection or a financing promise?
transfer_conditions.what_evidence_is_missing: A buyer or partner letter, fee schedule, invoice-to-collection trail, arrears ageing and capital-loss owner.

transfer_conditions.anchor_observation: Rightmove shows recurring professional ARPA; 99acres shows billing scale with a reported operating loss; Pinhome does not disclose a clean payer or margin split.
transfer_conditions.bangladesh_question: Which local customer will pay for a defined outcome before a national audience exists?
transfer_conditions.what_evidence_is_missing: A paid pilot, acquisition cost, lead quality definition, renewal decision and contribution after human service cost.

transfer_conditions.anchor_observation: A parent-backed venture could have captive supply, but the same relationship can weaken neutrality for rival developers and agents.
transfer_conditions.bangladesh_question: Can a venture state access, ranking, data-use and conflict rules that outside participants will accept?
transfer_conditions.what_evidence_is_missing: A governance policy, non-parent pilot, participation test and evidence that a rival payer renews.

supports: The payer and workflow, not the interface label, are the unit of comparison.
Professional recurring spend can support a portal, but audience and billing scale do not guarantee profit.
Human coordination, records and partner obligations remain part of the work even when discovery is digital.
Adjacent services and finance should be treated as separate operating systems with separate owners and metrics.
contradicts: There is no evidence here for one universal property technology model.
Foreign scale, company-reported activity and funding do not transfer into Bangladesh unit economics by themselves.
The chapter does not support a brokerage-first verdict, a national marketplace forecast or a capital-heavy launch.
cannot_infer: Whether a JCX-backed venture has repeatable collected commission today.
Whether a Bangladesh bank, developer or agent will pay for a specific product.
Whether a parent-backed marketplace can remain neutral enough to attract outside supply.
Whether JCX's internal technology adoption will follow any one external developer precedent.
